context_of_use: Comparative synthetic engineering evidence for ECG R-peak detection and beat-to-beat RR robustness across a paired, escalating composite noise frontier.
evidence_boundary: Synthetic comparative R-peak and beat-to-beat RR engineering evidence only; the SNR ladder is not a patient-noise prevalence model, clinical validation, diagnostic performance evidence, or regulatory qualification.

evidence_profile.description: A demanding engineering gate for high-performing implementations and additional regression headroom. It is not clinical evidence.
evidence_profile.threshold_adjustment: Relative to Level 2: minimum gates are increased by 0.05 (ceiling 1); maximum error gates are multiplied by 0.75.

truth_policy.aggregation: Each SNR case has its own acceptance stratum. Pooled results cannot compensate for a failed tier.
truth_policy.event_scoreability: All additive calibrated-noise, baseline-wander and powerline intervals remain scoreable. Only physically truncated record-boundary QRS truth is excluded.
truth_policy.first_beat: Excluded because no preceding in-record R peak exists for RR construction.
truth_policy.paired_design: The eight noisy scenarios use the same cardiac timebase, deterministic PVC cadence, interval schedule and noise source offsets; only target SNR and analytic artifact severities increase.
truth_policy.rr_definition: Difference between consecutive present-QRS construction R-peak times inside the record; an interval touching unscoreable R-peak truth is not_evaluable.
truth_policy.scope: R-peak event and RR measurement files are required. Signal-quality labels and HRV are explicitly outside the evidence matrix.
truth_policy.snr_definition: Target SNR is 20 log10(clean AC RMS / added-noise RMS), calibrated independently for every selected lead and interval. More-negative values are harder.
truth_policy.threshold_basis: Thresholds are a monotone, pre-specified engineering policy for this exact composite synthetic protocol. They are not universal clinical, classical-algorithm or deep-learning performance claims.
